entities.summary: Giottino, also known as Tommaso Fiorentino, was an early Italian painter from Florence. He was born in the late 14th century but the exact date is unknown. His real name was Maso di Stefano or Tommaso di Stefano. Giottino was a prominent artist of the Early Renaissance, active in the 1370s and 1380s. He is best known for his altarpieces and frescoes in the Florentine churches of Santa Maria del Carmine and Santa Maria Novella. Giottino's work was heavily influenced by the International Gothic style, and he was one of the first artists to use the sfumato technique. His paintings often featured dreamlike landscapes and figures, showcasing his mastery of light and shadow. Giottino's legacy can be seen in the works of later Renaissance artists, including Masaccio and Brunelleschi. He was a key figure in the development of the Florentine school of painting, which would go on to influence artists across Europe. Giottino's frescoes in Santa Maria Novella are considered some of the most beautiful and intricate in all of Florence. Despite his significant contributions to the art world, Giottino's life and work are not as well-documented as those of his contemporaries. His paintings have survived the test of time, however, and continue to be celebrated for their beauty and historical significance.
